newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam's rice prices mirror currency decline.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam's rice prices mirror currency decline.

text.p: Vietnam's export rice prices continued to fall this week in active trade mirroring a slide in the value of the local currency, the dong, dealers said on Thursday. Five percent broken grade was being quoted in Ho Chi Minh City at $263-$265 per tonne FOB Saigon Port, about three dollars lower than last week.
Ten percent broken was changing hands at around the $255 mark, but domestic prices in southern Vietnam's Mekong Delta, the main producing area, remained unchanged.
Vietnam's currency has fallen by around four percent in value over the past 10 days on the interbank market after the central bank moved to widen the official trading band.
The move was interpreted by analysts as a measure aimed at tackling Hanoi's ballooning trade deficit by making exports cheaper and imports more expensive.
Traders said 11 vessels were currently in Saigon Port. Buyers over the last week were reported in the Philippines, Malaysia, Indonesia and Cuba.
Farmers in the Mekong Delta have begun harvesting the winter-spring crop within the past couple of weeks. The crop is normally the highest-quality harvest of the year.
